defCn: 垃圾回收器，自动回收堆中不再被引用对象所占内存的 JVM 组件
defEn: A component of the JVM that automatically reclaims memory occupied by unreachable objects.
codeExample: System.gc(); // suggests (but does not force) GC
exampleSentence: The garbage collector paused the application to reclaim unreachable objects.
exampleSentences: The garbage collector paused the application to reclaim unreachable objects.
Tuning the collector is mostly about understanding object lifetimes.
A low-pause collector keeps tail latency predictable under load.

defCn: 堆，JVM 中线程共享、存放对象实例的内存区域，由垃圾回收器管理
defEn: The thread-shared runtime memory area where Java objects are allocated and reclaimed by the GC.
codeExample: Object o = new Object(); // allocated on the heap
exampleSentence: Most objects live on the heap, which is shared across all threads.
exampleSentences: Most objects live on the heap, which is shared across all threads.
A heap dump reveals which objects retain the most memory.
Tuning -Xmx controls the maximum heap size.

defCn: 栈帧，每次方法调用时在虚拟机栈中创建的结构，保存局部变量、操作数栈和返回地址
defEn: A per-method invocation record on the thread stack holding local variables, the operand stack, and the return address.
codeExample: void foo() { int x = 1; bar(); } // each call pushes a stack frame
exampleSentence: Each method call pushes a new stack frame that is popped when the method returns.
exampleSentences: Each method call pushes a new stack frame that is popped when the method returns.
Deep recursion eventually overflows the thread stack with too many frames.
Local variables live inside their own stack frame, not on the heap.

defCn: 元空间，JDK 8 起用于存储类元数据（字节码、类结构、静态变量）的本地内存区域
defEn: Native memory area (since JDK 8) holding class metadata such as bytecode and structure info, replacing PermGen.
exampleSentence: Metaspace holds class metadata and grows in native memory rather than the heap.
exampleSentences: Metaspace holds class metadata and grows in native memory rather than the heap.
Loading too many classes can exhaust metaspace and throw an OutOfMemoryError.
Unlike PermGen, metaspace is not fixed by default heap bounds.

defCn: Java 内存模型，规定多线程下共享变量的读写可见性与有序性规范的并发编程基础
defEn: The specification that defines visibility and ordering guarantees for shared-variable access across threads.
codeExample: // JMM defines when a write by one thread is visible to another
exampleSentence: The Java Memory Model defines when writes by one thread become visible to another.
exampleSentences: The Java Memory Model defines when writes by one thread become visible to another.
Without a happens-before edge, the JMM makes no visibility guarantee.
Reasoning about concurrency always anchors back to the JMM.

defCn: 先行发生，JMM 中描述两个操作之间可见性与顺序关系的偏序规则
defEn: A JMM partial-ordering rule guaranteeing that one action's results are visible to and ordered before another.
codeExample: // volatile write happens-before subsequent volatile read
exampleSentence: A volatile write happens-before every subsequent volatile read of the same field.
exampleSentences: A volatile write happens-before every subsequent volatile read of the same field.
Monitor unlock happens-before a later lock on the same monitor.
Chaining happens-before edges is how you prove a program is correctly synchronized.

defCn: 易变的，修饰变量以保证可见性与禁止特定重排序，但不保证复合操作的原子性
defEn: A keyword guaranteeing visibility of writes and ordering, but not atomicity for compound actions like i++.
exampleSentence: Marking a flag volatile makes a thread's write immediately visible to other threads.
exampleSentences: Marking a flag volatile makes a thread's write immediately visible to other threads.
Volatile prevents instruction reordering around the accessed variable.
It does not make a read-modify-write operation like i++ atomic.

defCn: 同步的，关键字通过监视器锁提供互斥与可见性，保证同一时刻仅一个线程进入临界区
defEn: A keyword providing mutual exclusion and visibility via a monitor lock on a block or method.
exampleSentence: The synchronized block lets only one thread execute the critical section at a time.
exampleSentences: The synchronized block lets only one thread execute the critical section at a time.
Releasing the monitor flushes all writes so the next acquirer sees them.
Use synchronized when you need both exclusion and a visibility guarantee.

defCn: 内存屏障，禁止处理器指令重排序并强制刷新/失效缓存的 CPU 指令，实现可见性与有序性
defEn: A CPU instruction that forbids certain reorderings and forces cache writes/reads, enabling visibility and ordering.
codeExample: // StoreStore barrier inserted after a volatile write
exampleSentence: Volatile access is implemented with memory barriers that stop the compiler and CPU from reordering.
exampleSentences: Volatile access is implemented with memory barriers that stop the compiler and CPU from reordering.
A StoreStore barrier forces prior writes to be flushed before a later store.
Memory barriers are the low-level mechanism behind happens-before.

defCn: 线程，JVM 中可独立调度执行的最小单位，每个线程拥有独立的程序计数器和栈
defEn: The smallest unit of execution in the JVM, each with its own program counter and stack.
codeExample: Thread t = new Thread(() -> work()); t.start();
exampleSentence: Each thread has a private stack but shares the heap with other threads.
exampleSentences: Each thread has a private stack but shares the heap with other threads.
Creating a raw thread per request can exhaust OS resources under load.
A thread in RUNNABLE may still be blocked on a socket read.

defCn: 虚拟线程，Project Loom 引入的轻量级 JVM 管理线程（Java 21），阻塞 I/O 时由载体线程卸载
defEn: A lightweight JVM-managed thread (Java 21) that unmounts from its carrier thread when blocked on I/O.
exampleSentence: Virtual threads let you run millions of concurrent tasks without sizing a thread pool.
exampleSentences: Virtual threads let you run millions of concurrent tasks without sizing a thread pool.
When a virtual thread blocks on I/O, the carrier OS thread is freed for another.
They are ideal for I/O-bound workloads that previously needed async callbacks.

defCn: 平台线程，映射到操作系统内核线程的传统重量级线程，创建成本高且有约 1MB 栈开销
defEn: A traditional heavyweight thread mapped one-to-one to an OS kernel thread, with roughly 1MB stack cost.
exampleSentence: Platform threads are expensive, so you typically limit them with a thread pool.
exampleSentences: Platform threads are expensive, so you typically limit them with a thread pool.
Each platform thread maps directly to an OS kernel thread.
High concurrency with platform threads leads to context-switch overhead.

defCn: 竞态条件，多个线程对共享状态的非原子访问导致结果依赖执行时序的缺陷
defEn: A defect where the outcome depends on the uncontrolled timing of concurrent accesses to shared state.
codeExample: // two threads run counter++ concurrently -> lost updates
exampleSentence: A race condition lost updates because the increment was not atomic.
exampleSentences: A race condition lost updates because the increment was not atomic.
Most race conditions vanish once you protect the shared state correctly.
Detecting races often means reasoning about every read-modify-write path.

defCn: 死锁，多个线程互相等待对方持有的锁而无法推进的状态
defEn: A state where two or more threads wait forever for locks held by each other, making no progress.
codeExample: // thread A holds lockX wants lockY; thread B holds lockY wants lockX
exampleSentence: The deadlock occurred because threads acquired locks in opposite orders.
exampleSentences: The deadlock occurred because threads acquired locks in opposite orders.
A thread dump can reveal a Java-level deadlock cycle.
Acquiring locks in a global order prevents circular waits.

defCn: 活锁，线程持续响应彼此状态而反复重试，虽未阻塞却始终无法推进
defEn: A situation where threads keep reacting to each other and retrying, never blocking yet never progressing.
codeExample: // two threads keep yielding to each other and restart
exampleSentence: The workers fell into a livelock, endlessly backing off and retrying.
exampleSentences: The workers fell into a livelock, endlessly backing off and retrying.
Unlike a deadlock, the threads are running but accomplish nothing.
Randomized backoff helps break a livelock loop.

defCn: 线程池，复用有限数量线程来执行大量任务的并发结构，控制并发度并提供队列与拒绝策略
defEn: A pool that reuses a bounded set of threads to run tasks, capping concurrency and offering queues and rejection policies.
exampleSentence: A thread pool caps concurrency and reuses threads instead of creating one per task.
exampleSentences: A thread pool caps concurrency and reuses threads instead of creating one per task.
A bounded queue with a rejection policy gives natural backpressure.
Sizing the pool depends on whether work is CPU-bound or I/O-bound.

defCn: 执行器服务，java.util.concurrent 中解耦任务提交与执行策略的接口，返回 Future 并管理生命周期
defEn: A java.util.concurrent interface decoupling task submission from execution policy, returning Futures and managing lifecycle.
exampleSentence: ExecutorService separates task submission from how and when tasks actually run.
exampleSentences: ExecutorService separates task submission from how and when tasks actually run.
Calling shutdown() lets in-flight tasks finish before the pool stops.
It returns a Future you can use to wait for a result.

defCn: 线程池执行器，可显式配置核心/最大线程数、空闲存活、工作队列与拒绝策略的线程池实现
defEn: The configurable ThreadPool implementation exposing core/max threads, keep-alive, work queue, and rejection handler.
exampleSentence: ThreadPoolExecutor lets you tune pool size, queue, and rejection policy explicitly.
exampleSentences: ThreadPoolExecutor lets you tune pool size, queue, and rejection policy explicitly.
Prefer it over Executors factory methods so limits are visible.
A bounded queue plus CallerRunsPolicy applies backpressure under load.

defCn: 可重入锁，比 synchronized 更灵活的可重入互斥锁，支持可中断、超时、公平性与条件变量
defEn: A reentrant mutual-exclusion lock offering features beyond synchronized: interruptible, timed, fair locks and conditions.
exampleSentence: ReentrantLock lets you attempt a lock with a timeout and back off gracefully.
exampleSentences: ReentrantLock lets you attempt a lock with a timeout and back off gracefully.
Always release it in a finally block to avoid leaking the lock.
Use it when you need condition variables or a fair locking policy.

defCn: 读写锁，允许多个读线程并发、写线程独占的锁，适合读多写少场景
defEn: A lock allowing concurrent readers but exclusive writers, suited to read-heavy workloads.
exampleSentence: ReadWriteLock improved throughput because many threads read without blocking each other.
exampleSentences: ReadWriteLock improved throughput because many threads read without blocking each other.
A write lock is exclusive and waits for all readers to finish.
It shines when reads vastly outnumber writes.

defCn: 倒计时门闩，使一个或多个线程等待直到其他线程完成 N 个事件的同步辅助类
defEn: A synchronizer that lets threads wait until a set of N operations completes via countDown().
exampleSentence: The main thread blocked on the CountDownLatch until all workers finished.
exampleSentences: The main thread blocked on the CountDownLatch until all workers finished.
Each worker calls countDown() when its task is done.
It is a one-shot barrier and cannot be reset.

defCn: 循环屏障，让一组线程在公共屏障点反复等待彼此到达的可重用同步器
defEn: A reusable barrier where a fixed set of threads wait for each other at a common point, repeatedly.
exampleSentence: The CyclicBarrier let four threads synchronize at the start of each iteration.
exampleSentences: The CyclicBarrier let four threads synchronize at the start of each iteration.
Unlike a latch, it resets and can be reused.
If a thread times out, the barrier is broken for the others.

defCn: 信号量，控制同时访问某资源的线程数量、通过许可获取与释放进行限流的同步器
defEn: A synchronizer limiting concurrent access to a resource by acquiring and releasing permits.
codeExample: Semaphore sem = new Semaphore(10); sem.acquire(); try { ... } finally { sem.release(); }
exampleSentence: A semaphore capped the number of concurrent database connections to ten.
exampleSentences: A semaphore capped the number of concurrent database connections to ten.
Acquire a permit before entering the limited resource and release it after.
It is a classic tool for throttling and bounded resource pools.

defCn: 可完成未来，支持异步任务组合（thenApply、thenCompose、allOf 等）的 Future 实现
defEn: A Future implementation enabling composable asynchronous pipelines such as thenApply, thenCompose, and allOf.
exampleSentence: CompletableFuture chained the fetch, transform, and aggregation steps without blocking.
exampleSentences: CompletableFuture chained the fetch, transform, and aggregation steps without blocking.
You can combine several with allOf or anyOf.
The exceptionally() stage handles failures declaratively.

defCn: 并发哈希表，采用分段/细粒度锁实现高并发读写、无锁读且线程安全的 Map 实现
defEn: A thread-safe Map using fine-grained locking so reads are lock-free and concurrent writes scale well.
exampleSentence: ConcurrentHashMap gave higher throughput than a synchronized map under contention.
exampleSentences: ConcurrentHashMap gave higher throughput than a synchronized map under contention.
Reads never block, even while writes are in progress.
It is the go-to concurrent map in most services.

defCn: 原子类，java.util.concurrent.atomic 中基于 CAS 实现无锁线程安全读-改-写操作的类（如 AtomicInteger）
defEn: A lock-free class in java.util.concurrent.atomic (e.g. AtomicInteger) providing safe read-modify-write via CAS.
exampleSentence: The atomic class updated the counter without any explicit lock.
exampleSentences: The atomic class updated the counter without any explicit lock.
AtomicReference lets you swap object references atomically.
They rely on compare-and-swap rather than mutual exclusion.

defCn: 比较并交换，CPU 原子指令，仅当内存值与预期值相等时才更新，是无锁算法的基础
defEn: A CPU atomic instruction that updates a value only if it still equals the expected one, underpinning lock-free algorithms.
exampleSentence: Compare-and-swap retries the update until no other thread changed the value first.
exampleSentences: Compare-and-swap retries the update until no other thread changed the value first.
It avoids locks but can suffer from contention under heavy writes.
Atomic classes expose CAS through compareAndSet.

defCn: 抽象队列同步器，java.util.concurrent 锁与同步器（ReentrantLock、Semaphore 等）的底层框架
defEn: The low-level framework (AQS) behind ReentrantLock, Semaphore, and other JUC synchronizers.
codeExample: // ReentrantLock, Semaphore, CountDownLatch all build on AQS
exampleSentence: AbstractQueuedSynchronizer provides the waiting queue that powers ReentrantLock.
exampleSentences: AbstractQueuedSynchronizer provides the waiting queue that powers ReentrantLock.
Most JUC locks subclass AQS and implement its state management.
Understanding AQS clarifies how fairness and blocking work.

defCn: 监视器，与每个对象关联的互斥锁，synchronized 进入/退出即获取/释放该监视器
defEn: The mutual-exclusion lock associated with every Java object, acquired and released by synchronized.
exampleSentence: Entering a synchronized block means acquiring the object's monitor.
exampleSentences: Entering a synchronized block means acquiring the object's monitor.
Only one thread may hold a given monitor at a time.
The monitor exit establishes a happens-before edge for the next acquirer.

defCn: 类加载器，负责将 .class 字节码加载为 JVM 中运行时类，遵循双亲委派模型
defEn: A component that loads .class bytecode into runtime classes, following the parent-delegation model.
exampleSentence: The classloader resolved the class from the classpath before the JVM could use it.
exampleSentences: The classloader resolved the class from the classpath before the JVM could use it.
The bootstrap, platform, and application loaders form a delegation chain.
Custom loaders enable hot reload and module isolation.

defCn: 字节码，Java 编译器生成的与平台无关的 .class 中间指令，由 JVM 解释或 JIT 编译执行
defEn: The platform-independent .class instruction set produced by the Java compiler and run by the JVM.
exampleSentence: The JVM executes bytecode either by interpreting it or compiling it to native code.
exampleSentences: The JVM executes bytecode either by interpreting it or compiling it to native code.
Bytecode is what makes Java write-once-run-anywhere.
Tools like ASM can generate or rewrite bytecode directly.

defCn: 即时编译器，JVM 在运行时将热点字节码路径编译为本地机器码以提升性能
defEn: The JVM component that compiles frequently executed ('hot') bytecode paths to native machine code at runtime.
codeExample: // hot methods get compiled to native code by the JIT
exampleSentence: The JIT compiler turned the hot loop into native code after enough executions.
exampleSentences: The JIT compiler turned the hot loop into native code after enough executions.
Profiling-driven compilation is why warm-up matters for benchmarks.
It balances startup speed against peak throughput.

defCn: 分代垃圾回收，基于弱分代假说将堆分为新生代与老年代、分别采用不同回收策略
defEn: A GC strategy splitting the heap into young and old generations based on object lifetime assumptions.
codeExample: // most objects die young -> collected in the young generation
exampleSentence: Generational garbage collection collects short-lived objects cheaply in the young generation.
exampleSentences: Generational garbage collection collects short-lived objects cheaply in the young generation.
Objects that survive several collections are promoted to the old generation.
It exploits the observation that most objects die young.

defCn: 新生代，堆中存放新创建对象的分代区域，分为 Eden 与两个 Survivor 区，Minor GC 在此进行
defEn: The heap region (Eden plus Survivor spaces) where new objects are allocated and collected by Minor GC.
codeExample: // new objects first land in Eden
exampleSentence: New objects are allocated in the young generation's Eden space.
exampleSentences: New objects are allocated in the young generation's Eden space.
A Minor GC copies survivors between the two Survivor spaces.
Tuning the young generation affects how often Minor GCs run.

defCn: 老年代，堆中存放经过多次回收仍存活对象的分代区域，由 Major/Full GC 回收
defEn: The heap region holding objects that survived multiple young-generation collections, reclaimed by Major/Full GC.
codeExample: // long-lived objects are promoted to the old generation
exampleSentence: Long-lived objects are eventually promoted into the old generation.
exampleSentences: Long-lived objects are eventually promoted into the old generation.
Collections there are slower and cause longer pauses.
A growing old generation often signals a memory leak.

defCn: G1 垃圾回收器，JDK 9 起默认的分Region回收器，优先回收垃圾最多的区域并支持可配置停顿目标
defEn: The default GC since JDK 9, dividing the heap into regions and prioritizing the ones with most garbage, with a pause goal.
exampleSentence: The G1 collector met our pause-time target by reclaiming the garbage-richest regions first.
exampleSentences: The G1 collector met our pause-time target by reclaiming the garbage-richest regions first.
It replaced fixed generations with equal-sized regions.
G1 suits heaps from a few GB up to tens of GB.

defCn: Z 垃圾回收器，低延迟 GC（JDK 15+），利用着色指针与读屏障实现亚毫秒级停顿、与堆大小无关
defEn: A low-latency GC (JDK 15+) using colored pointers and load barriers for sub-millisecond pauses regardless of heap size.
exampleSentence: ZGC kept pauses under a millisecond even on a multi-terabyte heap.
exampleSentences: ZGC kept pauses under a millisecond even on a multi-terabyte heap.
It does most GC work concurrently with the application.
The trade-off is higher CPU overhead than G1.

defCn: Shenandoah 垃圾回收器，低停顿并发 GC，通过 Brooks 指针与读屏障在应用运行同时压缩堆
defEn: A low-pause concurrent GC that compacts the heap concurrently with the application using forwarding pointers and barriers.
exampleSentence: Shenandoah reduced pause times by compacting the heap concurrently with the app.
exampleSentences: Shenandoah reduced pause times by compacting the heap concurrently with the app.
It targets predictable low latency like ZGC.
Concurrent compaction avoids the long stop-the-world pauses of older collectors.

defCn: CMS 并发标记清除回收器，老年代的并发低停顿收集器，已废弃，易产生内存碎片
defEn: The deprecated Concurrent Mark-Sweep collector for the old generation, low-pause but prone to fragmentation.
exampleSentence: The legacy CMS collector was replaced by G1 and ZGC in modern JDKs.
exampleSentences: The legacy CMS collector was replaced by G1 and ZGC in modern JDKs.
It collected the old generation mostly concurrently with the application.
Its free-list fragmentation could force a full compaction pause.

defCn: 整堆回收，回收整个堆（含新生代与老年代）的耗时操作，常导致较长停顿
defEn: A collection of the entire heap (young and old generations) that typically causes the longest pauses.
codeExample: // a Full GC scans and compacts all generations
exampleSentence: Frequent Full GCs pointed to a memory leak filling the old generation.
exampleSentences: Frequent Full GCs pointed to a memory leak filling the old generation.
A Full GC pauses all application threads.
Reducing promotion pressure lowers Full GC frequency.

defCn: 停顿，垃圾回收或某些操作时暂停所有应用线程以保证一致性的阶段
defEn: A phase during which all application threads are paused so the JVM can perform a consistent operation like GC.
codeExample: // GC pause: all mutator threads stop
exampleSentence: The stop-the-world pause froze every thread while the collector relocated objects.
exampleSentences: The stop-the-world pause froze every thread while the collector relocated objects.
Low-latency collectors minimize these pauses via concurrency.
Long stop-the-world times directly hurt request tail latency.

defCn: 内存溢出错误，JVM 无法分配更多内存时抛出的严重错误，常由泄漏或堆/元空间设置过小引起
defEn: A fatal error thrown when the JVM cannot allocate further memory, often from leaks or undersized heap/metaspace.
exampleSentence: The service crashed with an OutOfMemoryError after a cache grew without bound.
exampleSentences: The service crashed with an OutOfMemoryError after a cache grew without bound.
Heap dumps help locate the objects retaining memory.
Metaspace exhaustion can also trigger this error.

defCn: 栈溢出错误，线程栈深度超过限制（如无限递归）时抛出的错误
defEn: An error thrown when a thread's stack depth exceeds its limit, typically from unbounded recursion.
exampleSentence: Unbounded recursion triggered a StackOverflowError on the calling thread.
exampleSentences: Unbounded recursion triggered a StackOverflowError on the calling thread.
Each recursive call consumes one more stack frame.
Raising -Xss delays but does not fix the underlying loop.

defCn: 线程局部变量，为每个线程提供独立变量副本，常用于连接池/请求上下文，但需防止在线程池中泄漏
defEn: A variable giving each thread its own isolated copy, useful for per-thread state like request context or connections.
codeExample: private static final ThreadLocal<Connection> conn = new ThreadLocal<>();
exampleSentence: ThreadLocal stored the user context so each request saw its own value.
exampleSentences: ThreadLocal stored the user context so each request saw its own value.
Always remove() it in a finally block when using a thread pool.
Leaked ThreadLocals can retain objects for the pool's lifetime.

defCn: 未来结果，代表异步计算尚未完成结果的句柄，可通过 get() 阻塞等待结果
defEn: A handle to the result of an asynchronous computation that you can block on with get().
codeExample: Future<Integer> f = executor.submit(task); Integer r = f.get();
exampleSentence: The Future let the caller retrieve the computation result once it finished.
exampleSentences: The Future let the caller retrieve the computation result once it finished.
Calling get() blocks until the task completes or fails.
CompletableFuture extends it with composable callbacks.

defCn: 分支合并池，基于工作窃取的线程池，适合递归分治（如并行 Stream）任务
defEn: A work-stealing thread pool suited to recursive divide-and-conquer tasks such as parallel Streams.
exampleSentence: The ForkJoinPool split the workload and let idle threads steal tasks from busy ones.
exampleSentences: The ForkJoinPool split the workload and let idle threads steal tasks from busy ones.
Parallel Streams run on the common ForkJoinPool by default.
Work-stealing keeps all cores busy with little contention.

defCn: 不可变性，对象创建后状态不可更改，是编写线程安全代码的常用手段
defEn: The property that an object's state cannot change after construction, a key technique for thread safety.
codeExample: record Point(int x, int y) {} // immutable
exampleSentence: Immutability made the shared configuration safe to read from many threads.
exampleSentences: Immutability made the shared configuration safe to read from many threads.
Immutable objects need no locks for safe publication.
Records are a concise way to express immutable data.

defCn: 弱引用，不影响对象被垃圾回收的引用类型，常用于缓存与监听器的自动清理
defEn: A reference that does not prevent its referent from being garbage-collected, used for caches and listeners.
exampleSentence: A weak reference let the cache entry be collected once no strong references remained.
exampleSentences: A weak reference let the cache entry be collected once no strong references remained.
WeakHashMap uses weak keys to avoid memory leaks.
Soft and phantom references offer other collection semantics.

defCn: 双重检查锁定，延迟初始化单例的优化写法，必须用 volatile 才能正确发布对象
defEn: An optimization for lazy singleton initialization that is only correct when the field is declared volatile.
codeExample: if (instance == null) { synchronized (C.class) { if (instance == null) instance = new C(); } }
exampleSentence: Double-checked locking is broken without volatile because of possible instruction reordering.
exampleSentences: Double-checked locking is broken without volatile because of possible instruction reordering.
The volatile field prevents another thread seeing a partially constructed object.
Today, a holder class or enum singleton is often simpler.

defCn: 安全发布，通过 final 字段、volatile、锁或线程安全容器使对象对其他线程正确可见
defEn: Making an object visible to other threads correctly via final fields, volatile, locks, or thread-safe containers.
codeExample: private final Config config = load(); // safe publication via final
exampleSentence: Safe publication ensured every thread saw the fully constructed configuration object.
exampleSentences: Safe publication ensured every thread saw the fully constructed configuration object.
Without it, a reader may observe a partially built object.
Final fields and volatile both establish the needed happens-before edge.

defCn: 大 O 表示法，用于描述算法运行时间或空间随输入规模增长的渐近上界
defEn: A mathematical notation that describes the upper bound of an algorithm's growth in time or space as input size increases.
codeExample: for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) sum += a[i]; // O(n)

exampleSentences: sliding window reduces an O(n^2) scan to a single O(n) pass.
Sliding window reduces an O(n^2) scan to a single O(n) pass.
Longest substring without repeating characters is solved with a sliding window.

defCn: 双指针，用两个索引在序列上相向或同向移动以高效求解的技巧
defEn: A technique using two indices moving through a sequence to solve pair or range problems.
codeExample: while (left < right) { if (sum == target) {...} else if (sum < target) left++; else right--; }
exampleSentence: two pointers turns a brute-force pair search into linear time on sorted input.
exampleSentences: two pointers turns a brute-force pair search into linear time on sorted input.
Two pointers turns a brute-force pair search into linear time on sorted input.
Valid palindrome is easily checked with two pointers from both ends.

defCn: 前缀和，预计算数组的累加和以便 O(1) 回答任意区间和的技巧
defEn: A precomputed running total that answers any range sum in constant time.
exampleSentence: prefix sum lets you query subarray sums in constant time after O(n) preprocessing.
exampleSentences: prefix sum lets you query subarray sums in constant time after O(n) preprocessing.
Prefix sum lets you query subarray sums in constant time after O(n) preprocessing.
Subarray sum equals K is a common prefix sum interview problem.

defCn: 贪心算法，每一步都做局部最优选择以期得到全局最优的方法
defEn: An approach that makes the locally optimal choice at each step, hoping for a global optimum.
exampleSentence: A greedy algorithm works only when local choices lead to a global optimum.
exampleSentences: A greedy algorithm works only when local choices lead to a global optimum.
Interval scheduling is solved optimally by a greedy algorithm.

defCn: 分治，将问题拆分为独立子问题递归求解再合并的策略
defEn: A strategy that splits a problem into independent subproblems, solves them, and combines results.
codeExample: mergeSort(a, l, r) { if(l>=r) return; m=(l+r)/2; ... }
exampleSentence: Merge sort and quicksort are textbook divide and conquer algorithms.
exampleSentences: Merge sort and quicksort are textbook divide and conquer algorithms.
Divide and conquer often leads to O(n log n) time bounds.

defCn: 位运算，直接使用与、或、异或、移位等位操作进行高效计算的技术
defEn: Techniques that use bitwise operators for compact, fast computation.
codeExample: int single = a[0]; for (int x : a) single ^= x;
exampleSentence: bit manipulation finds the unique number in linear time and constant space.
exampleSentences: bit manipulation finds the unique number in linear time and constant space.
Bit manipulation finds the unique number in linear time and constant space.
XOR is a favorite bit manipulation trick in coding interviews.

defCn: 快慢指针，两个指针以不同速度移动，用于链表找环或中点
defEn: Two pointers moving at different speeds, used to find cycles or the middle of a list.
codeExample: while (fast != null && fast.next != null) { slow = slow.next; fast = fast.next.next; }
exampleSentence: fast and slow pointers detect a cycle without extra memory.
exampleSentences: fast and slow pointers detect a cycle without extra memory.
Fast and slow pointers detect a cycle without extra memory.
We used fast and slow pointers to locate the middle node of a linked list.

defCn: Kadane 算法，用动态规划在线性时间内求最大子数组和的算法
defEn: A linear-time DP algorithm that finds the maximum sum of a contiguous subarray.
exampleSentence: Kadane's algorithm finds the maximum subarray sum in a single pass.
exampleSentences: Kadane's algorithm finds the maximum subarray sum in a single pass.
Maximum subarray is the canonical application of Kadane's algorithm.

defCn: 可扩展性，指系统在负载（用户、数据、流量）增长时仍能维持性能的能力
defEn: The ability of a system to handle growing amounts of work by adding resources.
codeExample: Design for scalability from day one, not after traffic spikes.
exampleSentence: Horizontal scalability is a core requirement for any system serving millions of users.
exampleSentences: Horizontal scalability is a core requirement for any system serving millions of users.
Vertical scalability hits a ceiling when you reach the largest available machine.

defCn: 水平扩展，通过增加更多机器（横向加节点）来分担负载，理论上无限扩展
defEn: Adding more machines to a system to distribute load, also called scaling out.
codeExample: We scaled out by adding 10 app servers behind a load balancer.
exampleSentence: Horizontal scaling is preferred for large distributed systems because it avoids a single point of failure.
exampleSentences: Horizontal scaling is preferred for large distributed systems because it avoids a single point of failure.
Google Search runs across thousands of commodity machines through horizontal scaling.

defCn: 垂直扩展，通过给单一服务器增加更多 CPU、内存或磁盘来提升性能
defEn: Adding more power (CPU, RAM, disk) to an existing machine, also called scaling up.
codeExample: Vertical scaling meant upgrading from 16GB to 128GB of RAM on the DB box.
exampleSentence: Vertical scaling is simple but has a hardware ceiling and creates a single point of failure.
exampleSentences: Vertical scaling is simple but has a hardware ceiling and creates a single point of failure.
We chose vertical scaling first because it required no code changes.

defCn: 负载均衡，将 incoming 请求分布到多台服务器以避免单点过载
defEn: Distributing incoming network traffic across multiple servers to avoid overload.
codeExample: Requests are spread across API servers behind an AWS ELB load balancer.
exampleSentence: Load balancing keeps the system responsive when millions of users log in at once.
exampleSentences: Load balancing keeps the system responsive when millions of users log in at once.
A round-robin algorithm is the simplest form of load balancing.

defCn: 负载均衡器，把流量分发到多台后端服务器的组件（如 Nginx、ELB）
defEn: A component that distributes traffic across backend servers; L4 routes on IP/port, L7 on HTTP content.
codeExample: An L7 load balancer routes by HTTP path and cookie, while L4 routes by IP and port.
exampleSentence: The load balancer sits in front of the cluster and routes requests to healthy nodes.
exampleSentences: The load balancer sits in front of the cluster and routes requests to healthy nodes.
We use an L7 load balancer so we can route by URL path.

defCn: 缓存，把频繁访问的数据放在更快的存储（内存）中以缩短响应并降低数据库压力
defEn: Storing frequently accessed data in fast storage to serve it quicker and reduce DB load.
codeExample: Twitter timelines are cached in Redis so the home feed loads in milliseconds.
exampleSentence: Caching is often the single biggest lever for improving read latency.
exampleSentences: Caching is often the single biggest lever for improving read latency.
The hardest part of caching is invalidation, not storage.

defCn: 旁路缓存（懒加载）模式：应用先查缓存，未命中再查数据库并回写缓存
defEn: A caching pattern where the app checks the cache, loads from DB on a miss, and writes the result back.
exampleSentence: Cache-aside is the most common pattern because it keeps the cache simple and lazy.
exampleSentences: Cache-aside is the most common pattern because it keeps the cache simple and lazy.
With cache-aside, a cache miss triggers a database read and then a cache write.

defCn: 写穿策略：数据同时写入缓存和数据库，保证缓存与数据库一致但写延迟较高
defEn: A write strategy that writes to the cache and the database simultaneously for strong consistency.
exampleSentence: Write-through trades higher write latency for always-consistent cached data.
exampleSentences: Write-through trades higher write latency for always-consistent cached data.
Because writes hit the DB immediately, write-through avoids cache miss penalties on read.

defCn: 写回策略：先写缓存，由缓存异步刷回数据库，写极快但有数据丢失风险
defEn: A write strategy that writes to the cache first and flushes to the database asynchronously.
codeExample: cache.set(key, val);  // flushed to DB later by the cache
exampleSentence: Write-behind gives very fast writes but risks data loss if a cache node fails.
exampleSentences: Write-behind gives very fast writes but risks data loss if a cache node fails.
We only use write-behind for data like view counters where loss is acceptable.

defCn: 内容分发网络，把静态资源复制到全球边缘节点，让用户就近获取以降低延迟
defEn: A geographically distributed network of edge servers that caches content close to users.
codeExample: Video thumbnails are served from a CDN node close to the user's city.
exampleSentence: A CDN cuts latency and shields the origin server from bursts of static-asset requests.
exampleSentences: A CDN cuts latency and shields the origin server from bursts of static-asset requests.
When you open YouTube, thumbnails load from the nearest CDN edge node.

defCn: 非关系型数据库，适合灵活 schema、高写入吞吐和海量扩展（如 MongoDB、Redis、Cassandra）
defEn: Non-relational databases designed for flexible schemas, high throughput, and horizontal scale.
codeExample: Amazon uses DynamoDB, a NoSQL store, for billions of item lookups.
exampleSentence: We chose NoSQL because our access pattern is simple key-value lookups with no joins.
exampleSentences: We chose NoSQL because our access pattern is simple key-value lookups with no joins.
NoSQL databases like Cassandra favor availability and partition tolerance over strict consistency.

defCn: 分片，把一个大数据库按分片键拆分到多个节点，每个节点只存部分数据
defEn: Splitting a large dataset across multiple database nodes by a shard key so each holds a fraction.
codeExample: user_id % 4 decides which of the four shards stores a given user's row.
exampleSentence: Sharding is necessary once a single database can no longer hold or serve all the data.
exampleSentences: Sharding is necessary once a single database can no longer hold or serve all the data.
The whole sharding answer hinges on choosing a shard key that avoids hot spots.

defCn: 分区，把数据按范围、哈希或地理位置切分到不同存储，常与 sharding 互换使用
defEn: Dividing data into segments by range, hash, or geography across storage nodes.
codeExample: Range partitioning puts users 1-1M on shard A and 1M-2M on shard B.
exampleSentence: Partitioning lets a cluster store more data than any single node could hold.
exampleSentences: Partitioning lets a cluster store more data than any single node could hold.
Hash partitioning spreads load evenly but makes range queries hit every partition.

defCn: 复制，在多个节点保存数据副本以提高可靠性和读扩展能力
defEn: Keeping multiple copies of data across nodes for reliability and read scaling.
codeExample: Writes go to the primary; replicas in other AZs serve reads.
exampleSentence: Replication improves availability but introduces replication lag on read replicas.
exampleSentences: Replication improves availability but introduces replication lag on read replicas.
Amazon RDS keeps replicas in multiple availability zones for failover.

defCn: 复制延迟，主库写入后副本异步同步所需的时间，可能导致读到稍旧的数据
defEn: The delay before a replica catches up to the primary, which can serve slightly stale reads.
codeExample: A read replica 200ms behind the primary may show a just-completed order as missing.
exampleSentence: Replication lag means read replicas can serve data that is slightly out of date.
exampleSentences: Replication lag means read replicas can serve data that is slightly out of date.
We monitor replication lag and route consistency-critical reads to the primary.

defCn: CAP 定理：分布式系统中一致性、可用性、分区容错三者最多只能同时满足两个
defEn: The theorem that a distributed system can guarantee at most two of Consistency, Availability, Partition tolerance.
codeExample: Under a network partition you must choose CP (consistency) or AP (availability).
exampleSentence: The CAP theorem forces a trade-off between consistency and availability during a partition.
exampleSentences: The CAP theorem forces a trade-off between consistency and availability during a partition.
Banking systems pick CP, while social apps often pick AP under the CAP theorem.

defCn: 一致性，在分布式系统中指所有节点在同一时刻看到相同的数据
defEn: In distributed systems, the property that every read returns the most recent write.
codeExample: Strong consistency requires every node to see the same data at the same time.
exampleSentence: Banking apps prioritize consistency because account balances must always be correct.
exampleSentences: Banking apps prioritize consistency because account balances must always be correct.
Choosing consistency over availability means some requests are rejected during a partition.

defCn: 可用性，系统在每个请求下都能返回（可能是非最新）响应的程度
defEn: The degree to which a system remains operational and returns a response to every request.
codeExample: We target 99.9% availability over a 28-day window via redundant failover.
exampleSentence: Instagram likes can tolerate eventual delay, so availability is prioritized over strict consistency.
exampleSentences: Instagram likes can tolerate eventual delay, so availability is prioritized over strict consistency.
High availability usually means running redundant copies across multiple zones.

defCn: 分区容错，系统在网络发生分区（节点间失联）时仍能继续运行的能力
defEn: The ability of a system to keep operating despite network partitions between nodes.
codeExample: Because network partitions are inevitable, partition tolerance is non-negotiable in practice.
exampleSentence: Partition tolerance is a given in real networks, so you really choose between C and A.
exampleSentences: Partition tolerance is a given in real networks, so you really choose between C and A.
Designing for partition tolerance means assuming messages between nodes can be lost.

defCn: 最终一致性，停止写入后副本会收敛到同一值，但不保证读取时多旧
defEn: A consistency model guaranteeing replicas converge once writes stop, regardless of interim staleness.
codeExample: DynamoDB is AP: reads may be stale, but they are eventually consistent.
exampleSentence: Eventual consistency is fine for a like count but unacceptable for a bank balance.
exampleSentences: Eventual consistency is fine for a like count but unacceptable for a bank balance.
Cassandra trades strict consistency for availability through eventual consistency.

defCn: 强一致性，任何读都返回最近一次写入的结果，通常通过同步复制实现
defEn: A guarantee that every read returns the most recent successful write.
codeExample: PostgreSQL with synchronous replication provides strong consistency.
exampleSentence: Strong consistency is required for financial transfers where stale reads are dangerous.
exampleSentences: Strong consistency is required for financial transfers where stale reads are dangerous.
Achieving strong consistency often means paying a latency cost on every write.

defCn: 消息队列，在生产者与消费者之间做异步缓冲，解耦服务并吸收流量峰值
defEn: An asynchronous buffer between a fast producer and a slow consumer, decoupling services.
codeExample: User uploads video -> queue -> worker transcodes -> queue -> notify user.
exampleSentence: A message queue lets a spike of requests queue up instead of timing out the caller.
exampleSentences: A message queue lets a spike of requests queue up instead of timing out the caller.
Message queues decouple producers from consumers and enable background processing.

defCn: 发布-订阅模式，发布者向主题发事件，多个订阅者各自收到独立副本
defEn: A messaging pattern where publishers emit events to topics and subscribers get independent copies.
codeExample: A 'post-published' event fans out to notification, feed, and analytics subscribers.
exampleSentence: Pub/sub lets one event trigger updates in many independent downstream services.
exampleSentences: Pub/sub lets one event trigger updates in many independent downstream services.
Redis provides a simple pub/sub mechanism for lightweight real-time messaging.

defCn: Apache Kafka，高吞吐的分布式事件流平台，适合日志、流处理和事件溯源
defEn: A distributed event-streaming platform optimized for high-throughput, durable message logs.
codeExample: Kafka handles millions of messages per second and supports replay from a durable log.
exampleSentence: Kafka is ideal for event streaming and analytics pipelines because of its durability.
exampleSentences: Kafka is ideal for event streaming and analytics pipelines because of its durability.
We use Kafka to fan out a single event to many consumer groups.

defCn: RabbitMQ，传统消息代理，擅长任务队列、复杂路由和基于确认的低延迟投递
defEn: A traditional message broker optimized for task queues, complex routing, and reliable delivery.
codeExample: RabbitMQ routes jobs to competing workers with acknowledgment-based reliability.
exampleSentence: RabbitMQ is a good default for job queues and background task distribution.
exampleSentences: RabbitMQ is a good default for job queues and background task distribution.
Unlike Kafka, RabbitMQ focuses on low-latency task delivery rather than event replay.

defCn: 限流，限制客户端在单位时间内可发起的请求数，以保护系统并防止滥用
defEn: Capping how many requests a client may make per time window to protect the system.
codeExample: A gateway rate limiter allows 100 requests per minute per API key.
exampleSentence: Rate limiting protects backends from abuse and ensures fair usage across clients.
exampleSentences: Rate limiting protects backends from abuse and ensures fair usage across clients.
We enforce rate limiting at the API gateway rather than inside each service.

defCn: 令牌桶算法：桶按固定速率补充令牌，请求消耗令牌，无令牌则被拒，允许短时突发
defEn: A rate-limiting algorithm where tokens refill at a fixed rate; requests consume a token, allowing bursts.
codeExample: A bucket holds 100 tokens and refills 10 per second; bursts are allowed until empty.
exampleSentence: The token bucket algorithm allows short bursts while still enforcing an average rate.
exampleSentences: The token bucket algorithm allows short bursts while still enforcing an average rate.
We implemented distributed rate limiting with a token bucket stored in Redis.

defCn: 漏桶算法：请求进入队列，以固定速率处理，溢出则被拒绝，强制平滑输出
defEn: A rate-limiting algorithm where requests queue and are processed at a fixed rate; overflow is rejected.
codeExample: Requests drip out of the leaky bucket at a constant rate regardless of arrival spikes.
exampleSentence: The leaky bucket smooths traffic by processing requests at a constant rate.
exampleSentences: The leaky bucket smooths traffic by processing requests at a constant rate.
Unlike token bucket, leaky bucket does not permit bursts beyond its fixed drain rate.

defCn: 幂等性，操作无论执行一次还是多次都产生相同结果，使分布式重试安全
defEn: The property that an operation produces the same result whether applied once or many times.
codeExample: PUT /orders/1  // idempotent: retrying does not create a second order
exampleSentence: Idempotency keys prevent duplicate charges when a client retries a failed payment.
exampleSentences: Idempotency keys prevent duplicate charges when a client retries a failed payment.
Making the API idempotent lets clients safely retry requests without side effects.

defCn: 一致性哈希：把节点和键放在哈希环上，增删节点只重映射约 1/N 的键
defEn: Placing nodes and keys on a hash ring so adding or removing a node remaps only about 1/N of keys.
codeExample: A cache ring with consistent hashing moves few keys when a node is added.
exampleSentence: Consistent hashing lets you scale a cache or shard without remapping nearly all keys.
exampleSentences: Consistent hashing lets you scale a cache or shard without remapping nearly all keys.
It is the classic follow-up to 'how do you add nodes to a distributed cache?'

defCn: 微服务架构：把系统拆成多个小服务，各自独立部署、扩展并承担特定职责
defEn: An architecture of small, independently deployable services each with a specific responsibility.
codeExample: Auth, billing, and feed are separate microservices communicating over gRPC.
exampleSentence: Microservices enable independent scaling but add the overhead of service discovery.
exampleSentences: Microservices enable independent scaling but add the overhead of service discovery.
We migrated from a monolith to microservices to let teams deploy independently.

defCn: 单体架构：整个系统作为单一代码库部署为一个单元，开发简单但扩展困难
defEn: A single codebase deployed as one unit; simple to build initially but hard to scale at large.
codeExample: Our first product was a Rails monolith serving web, API, and jobs together.
exampleSentence: A monolith is simpler to develop and deploy until it becomes too large to scale.
exampleSentences: A monolith is simpler to develop and deploy until it becomes too large to scale.
Many teams start with a monolith and split into microservices only when needed.

defCn: API 网关：客户端请求的统一入口，负责路由、认证、限流和 SSL 终结
defEn: A single entry point for client requests handling routing, auth, rate limiting, and SSL termination.
codeExample: The API gateway validates JWTs and rate-limits before forwarding to services.
exampleSentence: An API gateway centralizes cross-cutting concerns like authentication and throttling.
exampleSentences: An API gateway centralizes cross-cutting concerns like authentication and throttling.
In a microservices setup the API gateway routes each request to the right service.

defCn: 服务发现：微服务架构中动态定位可用服务实例的机制（如 Consul、etcd）
defEn: Mechanism for dynamically locating available service instances in a microservices architecture.
codeExample: Services register with Consul so clients can discover healthy instances.
exampleSentence: Service discovery is essential once you have dynamic, autoscaled microservice instances.
exampleSentences: Service discovery is essential once you have dynamic, autoscaled microservice instances.
Without service discovery, clients would need hardcoded and brittle host addresses.

defCn: 断路器模式：下游持续失败时停止调用并快速失败，避免重试风暴和级联故障
defEn: A pattern that stops calling a failing dependency and fails fast during a cooldown to prevent cascades.
codeExample: After 5 timeouts, the circuit breaker opens and rejects calls for 30 seconds.
exampleSentence: A circuit breaker prevents retry storms from cascading failures across services.
exampleSentences: A circuit breaker prevents retry storms from cascading failures across services.
We added a circuit breaker so a slow payment provider cannot stall the checkout path.

defCn: 领导者选举：集群就一个协调节点达成一致，并在其失效时安全替换
defEn: How a cluster agrees on one coordinator node and safely replaces it on failure.
codeExample: Raft performs leader election so only one node accepts writes at a time.
exampleSentence: Leader election ensures exactly one node coordinates writes while the leader is healthy.
exampleSentences: Leader election ensures exactly one node coordinates writes while the leader is healthy.
Consensus algorithms like Raft handle leader election and failover automatically.

defCn: 法定人数：在 N 个副本中需 R 次读、W 次写确认且 R+W>N，保证读到最新写入
defEn: Requiring R reads and W writes from N replicas with R + W > N so reads overlap the latest write.
codeExample: With N=3, W=2, R=2, every read touches a replica that saw the latest write.
exampleSentence: A quorum system guarantees a read overlaps the most recent write across replicas.
exampleSentences: A quorum system guarantees a read overlaps the most recent write across replicas.
We tune quorum sizes to balance latency against consistency guarantees.

defCn: 数据库索引：把 O(n) 全表扫描变为 O(log n) 查找，代价是写变慢、存储增多
defEn: A data structure that turns O(n) scans into O(log n) lookups at the cost of slower writes.
codeExample: CREATE INDEX ON orders(user_id);  // speeds lookups, slows inserts
exampleSentence: Database indexing speeds up reads but slows writes and uses extra storage.
exampleSentences: Database indexing speeds up reads but slows writes and uses extra storage.
B-tree indexes are the workhorse behind most relational query optimization.

defCn: 分布式锁：在多个节点间协调互斥访问共享资源，常用 Redis 等实现
defEn: A lock that coordinates exclusive access to a resource across multiple nodes.
codeExample: acquire_lock('job-42') via Redis SET NX before processing a shared task.
exampleSentence: A distributed lock prevents two nodes from processing the same job simultaneously.
exampleSentences: A distributed lock prevents two nodes from processing the same job simultaneously.
Naive Redis locks need fencing tokens to avoid stale-lock race conditions.

defCn: 死信队列：消息处理失败 N 次后被转入的队列，便于排查和后续重放
defEn: A queue where messages are sent after failing processing a set number of times.
codeExample: After 5 failed attempts the message is routed to the dead letter queue.
exampleSentence: A dead letter queue isolates poison messages without blocking the main pipeline.
exampleSentences: A dead letter queue isolates poison messages without blocking the main pipeline.
We inspect the dead letter queue to find messages that repeatedly failed processing.

defCn: 扇出：一个事件触发向多个接收者投递或更新（写时扇出 vs 读时扇出）
defEn: A single event triggering delivery or updates to many recipients (write vs read fan-out).
codeExample: Fan-out-on-write pushes a post to every follower's feed at publish time.
exampleSentence: Feed design is fundamentally a trade-off between fan-out-on-write and fan-out-on-read.
exampleSentences: Feed design is fundamentally a trade-off between fan-out-on-write and fan-out-on-read.
A publish event fans out to notification, analytics, and search indexers.

defCn: 背压：下游处理不过来时通知上游放慢速度，而不是无限堆积直至崩溃
defEn: A mechanism telling upstream senders to slow down when a system cannot keep up.
codeExample: When the buffer is full, the consumer applies backpressure to the producer.
exampleSentence: Backpressure prevents a slow consumer from silently queueing work until the system collapses.
exampleSentences: Backpressure prevents a slow consumer from silently queueing work until the system collapses.
Kafka consumers signal backpressure by pausing their fetch loop under load.

defCn: 优雅降级：部分依赖失效时系统仍以降级模式运行，而非整体崩溃
defEn: Keeping partial service when dependencies fail, instead of crashing entirely.
codeExample: If recommendations fail, the app still lets users search and play saved songs.
exampleSentence: Graceful degradation keeps the app usable when a non-critical service is down.
exampleSentences: Graceful degradation keeps the app usable when a non-critical service is down.
We use cached or stale data as a fallback for graceful degradation.

defCn: 容错：系统在部分组件故障时仍能正确运行，通常通过冗余和副本实现
defEn: The ability of a system to keep operating correctly when some components fail.
codeExample: Replication and failover give the cluster fault tolerance against node loss.
exampleSentence: Fault tolerance is achieved through redundancy, replication, and automated failover.
exampleSentences: Fault tolerance is achieved through redundancy, replication, and automated failover.
Designing for fault tolerance means assuming any single node can die at any time.

defCn: 服务等级目标：对某可靠性指标在一段时间内的目标（如 28 天内 99.9% 请求 <300ms）
defEn: A target for a reliability metric over a window, implying an error budget.
codeExample: Our SLO is 99.9% of requests under 300ms measured over 28 days.
exampleSentence: An SLO defines the reliability target and the error budget a team is allowed to spend.
exampleSentences: An SLO defines the reliability target and the error budget a team is allowed to spend.
When we breach the SLO, the error budget is exhausted and releases are frozen.

defCn: Redis，内存键值数据库，常用作缓存、限流计数器和简单发布订阅
defEn: An in-memory key-value store commonly used for caching, rate-limit counters, and pub/sub.
codeExample: We cache sessions in Redis and use it to store token-bucket counters.

defCn: ACID 事务四属性：原子性、一致性、隔离性、持久性，关系型数据库的核心保证

exampleSentences: ACID guarantees make relational databases the right choice for financial records.
NoSQL stores often relax ACID for scalability and availability.

defCn: 事件溯源：把状态变化存为不可变的追加日志，而非只存当前状态
defEn: Storing state changes as an immutable, append-only sequence of events rather than current state.

exampleSentences: Event sourcing lets you reconstruct past states by replaying the immutable event log.
Combined with Kafka, event sourcing provides a durable audit trail.

defCn: 命令查询职责分离：把读模型（查询）与写模型（命令）分开，各自独立优化
defEn: Separating read (query) and write (command) models so each can be optimized independently.

exampleSentence: CQRS lets the read side scale independently from the write side of a system.
exampleSentences: CQRS lets the read side scale independently from the write side of a system.
We adopted CQRS to serve heavy read traffic from a tailored query model.

defCn: 精确一次语义：消息既不丢失也不重复，分布式系统中极难实现
defEn: A delivery guarantee that a message is processed neither lost nor duplicated, very hard to achieve.

exampleSentence: Exactly-once semantics are extremely difficult and usually approximated with idempotency.
exampleSentences: Exactly-once semantics are extremely difficult and usually approximated with idempotency.
Most brokers offer at-least-once and rely on consumers to dedupe for exactly-once.

defCn: 至少一次投递：消息可能重复但绝不丢失，常配合幂等消费去重
defEn: A delivery guarantee that a message may be duplicated but is never lost.
codeExample: SQS standard queues give at-least-once delivery, so consumers must dedupe.
exampleSentence: At-least-once delivery is common and safe as long as consumers are idempotent.
exampleSentences: At-least-once delivery is common and safe as long as consumers are idempotent.
Kafka provides at-least-once delivery by default on its durable log.

defCn: 负载卸载：系统过载时有意丢弃或拒绝低优先级请求以保住核心功能
defEn: Deliberately dropping or rejecting lower-priority requests when the system is overloaded.
codeExample: Under overload the gateway sheds batch jobs to keep interactive requests fast.
exampleSentence: Load shedding protects the core path by rejecting best-effort work during peaks.
exampleSentences: Load shedding protects the core path by rejecting best-effort work during peaks.
We combine rate limiting with load shedding to survive unexpected traffic spikes.

defCn: 尾延迟：系统最慢百分位（p95、p99）的延迟，多后端调用时极易被用户命中
defEn: The latency of a system's slowest percentiles (p95, p99), often hit by many backend calls.
codeExample: p99 latency was 800ms even though the median was only 40ms.
exampleSentence: Tail latency matters because a page makes many calls, so users often hit a p99-slow one.
exampleSentences: Tail latency matters because a page makes many calls, so users often hit a p99-slow one.
We cache aggressively to flatten tail latency on the critical path.

defCn: API 设计：定义服务与组件间清晰、高效通信的接口（REST、GraphQL、gRPC）
defEn: Defining clear, efficient interfaces for communication between services (REST, GraphQL, gRPC).

exampleSentences: API design is about clear contracts that make services easy to consume and evolve.

defCn: GraphQL，API 查询语言，客户端在单次请求中精确指定所需字段，避免超额获取

exampleSentences: GraphQL lets the client request exactly the data it needs, reducing over-fetching.

defCn: gRPC，Google 的 RPC 框架，使用 Protocol Buffers 二进制序列化，支持双向流
defEn: Google's RPC framework using binary Protocol Buffers over HTTP/2 with strong typing and streaming.
exampleSentence: gRPC is faster than JSON over REST for internal service-to-service calls.
exampleSentences: gRPC is faster than JSON over REST for internal service-to-service calls.
We use gRPC with Protobuf for typed, low-latency microservice communication.

defCn: 传输层安全协议，加密传输中的数据，是通信安全与合规的基础
defEn: Transport Layer Security, the protocol that encrypts data in transit.
codeExample: All traffic between services is encrypted with mutual TLS (mTLS).
exampleSentence: TLS encrypts data in transit and is the baseline for any secure API.
exampleSentences: TLS encrypts data in transit and is the baseline for any secure API.
We enforce mTLS so services authenticate each other on the network.

defCn: 可观测性：通过日志、指标、追踪获得系统内部运行状态的可见性
defEn: The ability to understand system internals via logs, metrics, and distributed tracing.

exampleSentence: Observability with logs, metrics, and tracing is how we debug systems at scale.
exampleSentences: Observability with logs, metrics, and tracing is how we debug systems at scale.
We added distributed tracing so a single request can be followed across services.

defCn: 共识：分布式节点就某一值或操作达成一致（如 Raft、Paxos）

codeExample: Raft achieves consensus by electing a leader that replicates a log.
exampleSentence: Consensus algorithms like Raft keep a replicated log consistent across nodes.
exampleSentences: Consensus algorithms like Raft keep a replicated log consistent across nodes.
We rely on consensus so the cluster agrees on which writes are committed.

defCn: 数据复制：将数据副本保存到多处以提高可用性与读扩展（主从/多主）
defEn: Keeping data copies across nodes for availability and read scaling (master-slave or multi-master).
codeExample: Master-slave replication sends writes to the master and reads to replicas.
exampleSentence: Data replication improves availability but introduces the challenge of conflict resolution.
exampleSentences: Data replication improves availability but introduces the challenge of conflict resolution.
Multi-master replication boosts write availability at the cost of merge conflicts.

defCn: 吞吐量：系统在单位时间内能处理的请求或数据量（如 QPS、msg/s）
defEn: The amount of work a system processes per unit of time, such as QPS or messages per second.
codeExample: Kafka sustains over 100K messages per second per broker.
exampleSentence: We size the cluster based on expected peak throughput, not average load.
exampleSentences: We size the cluster based on expected peak throughput, not average load.
Throughput and latency are often traded off against each other under load.

defCn: 延迟：一个请求从发起到收到响应所经历的时间
defEn: The time it takes for a request to travel and receive a response.
codeExample: Caching cuts read latency from 50ms to under 1ms.
exampleSentence: Latency, not just throughput, is what users feel when a system is slow.
exampleSentences: Latency, not just throughput, is what users feel when a system is slow.
We measure p50, p95, and p99 latency to capture the full distribution.

defCn: 高可用：通过冗余、副本和自动故障转移让系统长期保持可运行
defEn: Keeping a system operational over time via redundancy, replication, and automated failover.

exampleSentences: High availability is achieved by removing single points of failure across the stack.

defCn: 最流行的开源关系型数据库，常用于 Web 应用后端，默认存储引擎为 InnoDB

exampleSentences: We run MySQL behind the application to store user and order data.

exampleSentences: PostgreSQL handles both relational and document data through its JSONB type.

exampleSentences: MongoDB stores each user profile as a single flexible document.

defCn: 高可用、可线性扩展的宽列 NoSQL 数据库，适合海量写入与多数据中心部署

exampleSentences: Cassandra tolerates node failures without downtime thanks to its masterless design.

defCn: 零配置、单文件嵌入式的轻量关系型数据库，常用于移动端与本地应用

exampleSentences: The mobile app stores all local data in a single SQLite file.

defCn: 商用企业级关系型数据库，以高可靠、强一致与完备的企业特性著称
defEn: A commercial, enterprise-grade relational database known for reliability, strong consistency, and advanced features like RAC and partitioning.
exampleSentence: The bank migrated its core system to Oracle Database for its high availability.
exampleSentences: The bank migrated its core system to Oracle Database for its high availability.

defCn: 微软开发的关系型数据库管理系统，深度集成 .NET 生态与企业工具链

exampleSentences: Our internal dashboards are powered by SQL Server and its reporting services.

defEn: Amazon's fully managed key-value and document database offering single-digit millisecond performance and seamless horizontal scaling.
exampleSentence: DynamoDB scales automatically to handle millions of requests per second.
exampleSentences: DynamoDB scales automatically to handle millions of requests per second.

defCn: 基于 Lucene 的分布式搜索与分析引擎，常用于全文检索、日志与指标分析
defEn: A distributed search and analytics engine built on Lucene, widely used for full-text search, logging, and metrics.

exampleSentences: We indexed all articles in Elasticsearch to power fast full-text search.

defCn: 主流的图数据库，以节点-关系模型和 Cypher 查询语言高效处理关联密集型数据

exampleSentences: Neo4j makes it natural to traverse social connections without expensive joins.
Fraud detection benefits from its relationship-centric model.

defCn: MySQL 的默认存储引擎，支持事务、行级锁与 MVCC，底层使用聚簇 B+ 树索引
defEn: The default MySQL storage engine, providing transactions, row-level locking, and MVCC through clustered B+ tree indexes.

exampleSentences: InnoDB keeps the primary key in a clustered B+ tree with row data stored in leaves.

defEn: A column-oriented database management system built for OLAP workloads with extremely fast aggregation queries.

exampleSentences: ClickHouse scans billions of rows in seconds for our analytics dashboard.

exampleSentences: Every backend developer should be comfortable writing SQL by hand.

exampleSentences: A relational database enforces schema and referential integrity by design.

defCn: 数据库索引常用的平衡树结构，所有数据存于叶子节点并通过链表串联，利于范围查询

exampleSentences: A B+ tree lets both point lookups and range queries stay fast.

exampleSentences: For deep pages, keyset pagination scales far better than OFFSET.

defCn: 基于分词与倒排索引的搜索方式，支持关键词匹配、相关性排序与自然语言查询

exampleSentences: Full-text search returns the most relevant articles instead of exact matches only.

exampleSentences: Paxos underpins many strongly consistent storage systems despite its complexity.

defCn: 位于数据源前的快速存储层，缓存热点数据以降低延迟、减轻数据库压力

exampleSentences: A vector database finds the most similar documents by nearest-neighbor search.
